text: At McMaster University in Canada, isotope analysis has been conducted on bone material from three skeletons from Hrísbrú. This research is among the first isotope analysis done on skeletons from Iceland. Isotope measurements can show where individuals grew up. In the first years of a persons life, information about diet and other environmental conditions that are different between regions in the world collects in the bones and preserves mostly in teeth. For example, Iceland is geologically much younger than Norway and that has an influence on the minerals in the water. In this way it is possible to discover where people grew up. The three skeletons that have been analyzed for isotopes have shown that these individuals were all born and raised in Iceland.
